sut_family: integrate.simpson (composite Simpson quadrature) -- aligns with paper numerical-integration / quadrature primitives
cat: L*.acc accuracy-order (family i; Mode M; E*: higher-order method must be >= as accurate / observed order == claimed). Composite Simpson is documented as globally 4th order; with an EVEN number of samples (ODD number of intervals) the pre-fix 'avg' boundary blend uses a trapezoidal rule on the odd interval, dropping the GLOBAL observed order from 4 to 3 (order reduction). The fixed 'simpson' method (Cartwright parabolic correction) restores observed order 4.
fix_title: ENH: integrate.simpson: improve accuracy for even number of points (#18209)

mr_used: L*.acc accuracy-order (family i, E*, Mode M). Composite Simpson is claimed globally 4th order. (1) observed order p_obs (slope of log||err|| vs log h over an even-#points / odd-#intervals refinement) must match the claimed order 4 (operationalised as p_obs >= 3.6); equivalently (2) the higher-order method must be at least as accurate as the lower-order one at matched work: ||err(simpson)|| <= ||err(avg)|| at every refinement level. Mode M: the two methods compared are two implementations of the SAME Simpson integral on the SAME nodes -- the pre-fix default even='avg' (trapezoidal boundary blend) vs the post-fix default even='simpson' (Cartwright parabolic correction). Source = high-accuracy quad reference; follow-up = simpson at the version default.

THIS IS FAMILY i (E*), NOT FAMILY h: the quadrature CONVERGES in both versions (abs_err -> 0 monotonically as h -> 0, so the L*.conv / family-h relation HOLDS on both sides); the defect is purely in the accuracy ORDER / RATE -- pre achieves error ~ h^3 where the method is documented to be ~ h^4, an ORDER REDUCTION caused by the trapezoidal boundary term on the odd interval. The fix restores the h^4 rate. Mode M is explicit: the MR compares two implementations of the SAME Simpson integral on the SAME nodes (even='avg' boundary-blend method vs even='simpson' parabolic-correction method); the released default flipped from the faulty 'avg' to the correct 'simpson' at 1.10.1 -> 1.11.0, and that version bracket localises the lower-order side.
mode: M (inter-implementation): same Simpson integral, two methods (avg-blend vs simpson parabolic correction). Distinct from family h (mere convergence, both versions converge) and family j (exact representation-invariance / zero-tolerance equality); here the relation is an APPROXIMATE accuracy-ORDER partial order, not exact equality.
note: Fills the previously-GAP scipy x i (L*.acc / E* accuracy-order) cell in the UNIFIED_BLOCK_MODEL coverage matrix. The bug: scipy/integrate/_quadrature.py simpson() with an EVEN number of samples (ODD #intervals) handled the leftover interval with a TRAPEZOIDAL rule (lines val += 0.5*last_dx*(y[slice1]+y[slice2]) in the pre-fix even='avg'/'first'/'last' branches), injecting an O(h^3) boundary error into the otherwise O(h^4) composite sum and dropping the GLOBAL observed convergence order to 3. Commit 572a373aa added the Cartwright degree-matched 3-point parabolic correction (new even='simpson', made the default at 1.11.0), restoring observed order 4. HONESTY CAVEAT (documented, not hidden): the fix does NOT make Simpson exact on cubics with even #points (e.g. integral of x^3 on [0,9]: exact 1640.25; pre even='avg' npts=4 gives 1701.0, post even='simpson' npts=4 gives 1660.5 -- improved but still not exact), so this entry is framed strictly as an OBSERVED-CONVERGENCE-ORDER / accuracy-rate defect (h^3 vs h^4), NOT as a degree-of-exactness restoration. The clean, reproducible E* signal is the observed-order drop 4->3 and the matched-work error ordering POST<=PRE. numpy pinned to 1.26.4 in both venvs to isolate the scipy method change.
